name: LightGlue
plain: LightGlue (ETH Zurich, Microsoft; ICCV 2023) with ALIKED or DISK keypoints: sparse matching of two photos of one scene, as keypoints plus index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Apache-2.0 (LightGlue, DISK) and BSD-3-Clause (ALIKED) code and weights.
summary: LightGlue (Lindenberger, Sarlin and Pollefeys 2023): sparse feature matching. A keypoint detector-descriptor (ALIKED or DISK) finds up to 2048 keypoints per image at a 1024-pixel long side, and a transformer with self- and cross-attention, adaptive depth and point pruning matches them. Returns both keypoint sets, the index pairs of the matches and their confidence.

papers.title: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed

limitations: Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
No exportable module: the keypoint counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).

ALIKED-LightGlue has a fixed 768 x 1024 standalone FP32 TensorRT encoder measurement with TF32 disabled. Keypoint selection and LightGlue run in PyTorch. On 300 MegaDepth pairs, AUC@5 was 51.32 versus 49.75 portable FP32, with a worst paired pose error increase of 21.25 degrees.

Computing DISK descriptors only at selected keypoints also changed pose outcomes. On a 100-pair MegaDepth check, both the PyTorch and TensorRT sparse projections changed a previously solved pair from 25.78 degrees to the 90-degree failure value, despite identical detected keypoints.
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead. To reconstruct camera poses from an image folder with these matchers, see [structure from motion](../sfm.md).

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors.

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, 300 pairs at 768 x 1024, pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Both modes receive pairs resized to 768 x 1024. Map matched pixels to the calibrated evaluation coordinates and use the same RANSAC seed per pair.
